property_summary: For every deployment, owner() always returns a non-zero address (the deployer) in the reference contract; the mutant returns address(0) breaking this invariant for some inputs.

For every deployment caller X, the reference contract's owner() returns the deploying address X, whereas the mutant returns address(0) for some deployments, violating the invariant that owner() equals the deployer.

For any (fuzzed) address A passed to owner() as a call sender, the reference contract's owner() getter returns the deployed owner (nonzero) regardless of caller, while the mutant returns address(0) breaking the rule that owner() != address(0) for some callers; the test fuzzes a caller address and asserts that calling owner() does not return address(0).

For any (fuzzed) address caller, calling owner() on a freshly deployed reference C always returns a non-zero address (the stored owner), whereas the mutant returns address(0) for some callers; the test asserts owner() != address(0) after calling it (i.e. the call completes and returns a non-zero owner).

For any caller address, calling owner() on the correct contract always returns a non-zero address (the stored owner); the mutant returns address(0) for some callers, violating the non-zero-owner property.

For any caller and transaction context, the correct contract's owner() must always return the originally stored owner (the account that received initial ownership on construction), whereas the mutant returns tx.origin which can differ from the stored owner for calls relayed through other contracts (so the mutant violates this when a caller contract invokes owner()).

For any caller context, the reference contract's owner() always returns the address that was set as owner at construction (the deployer), while the mutant returns tx.origin which can differ when a contract calls owner(), so the mutant can produce a different value for some contract-caller inputs.

For any caller, the reference contract's owner() always returns the stored owner set at construction (the deployer), but the mutant returning tx.origin can differ when owner() is invoked via a calling contract (tx.origin becomes the original EOA), so a contract-caller can observe different owner() values between P and M.

For every caller address (EOA or contract), the reference contract's owner() returns the stored owner set at construction (the deployer); the mutant that returns tx.origin can return a different address when owner() is invoked through a calling contract, so there exists a contract-caller input that makes the return differ.

For any caller address, the reference contract's owner() always returns the stored owner set at construction (the deployer); the mutant that returns tx.origin can return a different address when owner() is invoked via a calling contract, so there exists a contract-caller input that makes owner()'s return differ (specifically when an intermediate contract calls owner()).

For every caller address x, the correct contract's owner() returns the stored owner (the deployer unless transferred) while the mutant incorrectly returns the immediate caller (msg.sender), so owner() must equal the original owner for all callers and the mutant will differ for at least some caller.

For any caller address, the deployed contract's owner() always returns the original stored owner (the deployer); the mutant returns msg.sender instead and thus will differ for callers other than the deployer.

For every caller address, calling owner() should always return the originally stored owner (the deployer) — the mutant returns the immediate caller (msg.sender) so for some fuzzed caller addresses the returned owner will differ.

For every caller address, the reference contract's owner() always returns the stored owner (the deployer); the mutant returns the immediate caller (msg.sender), so for some caller addresses the returned owner will differ from the stored deployer.
For every caller address, C.owner() must return the stored owner address (the deployer) — the mutant that returns msg.sender will sometimes return a different address when called by other addresses.

For every input, the contract's owner() getter must return the address that was set as owner on deployment (the deployer), but the mutant incorrectly returns the contract's own address, breaking this invariant for some inputs.

For every deployment caller, C.owner() returns the deployer address (the contract's recorded owner); the mutant instead returns address(this) breaking this for deployers not equal to the contract address (which are all EOAs), so there exist inputs where owner() differs.
For every deployment caller (any EOA address), C.owner() returns that deployer address; the mutant returns address(this) instead, so there exist deployer addresses for which owner() differs.

For every deployment sender, the contract's owner() returns the stored owner address (the deployer) — the mutant returning address(this) breaks this because address(this) != deployer for some fuzzed deployer addresses.

For every fuzzed caller address that deploys C (simulated by impersonation), C.owner() returns that deployer address (the stored owner); the mutant returns address(this) instead, so for some deployer addresses the returned owner differs.

For any deployer address, the deployed contract's owner() must return the deployer (the address that constructed C); the mutant that returns a constant address(1) violates this for many deployer addresses.
For any deployer address D, the contract's owner() should return D (the constructor's msg.sender); the mutant that always returns address(1) violates this for many deployer addresses.

For any caller address X used in setUp() via vm.prank before deploying C, the deployed contract's owner() must equal that deployer X; the mutant that returns address(1) breaks this when the deployer is not address(1).

For any caller A, calling owner() on the deployed contract returns the contract's recorded owner (the address stored in the Ownable state) — the mutant that returns address(1) can produce a different returned address for some deployer/caller choices, violating this invariant.

For any deployer address D used to construct C, the public owner() call returns the stored contract owner (the deployer); the mutant that returns address(1) can differ from that stored owner for many deployers, so there exist inputs where owner()'s return differs.
